verdict.rationale: Lium documents its own SDK on a dedicated sdk.md page that rents the cheapest matching node, runs a function, returns the result and removes the pod. That is a real first-party SDK for building against the platform. The evidence covers only one SDK, described in a single sentence, and its language, API surface and installation are not shown. The TypeScript path is generated types from an OpenAPI spec, which is a developer building block rather than an official SDK. missing for 10: evidence of multiple official SDKs across languages, in-depth SDK reference documentation (API surface, install, examples), independent or hands-on corroboration that the SDK works as described.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs the function there, returns the result and removes the pod (or keeps it warm).
